title: How to Pass EPUBCheck Before Uploading to Amazon
excerpt: EPUBCheck is the validation tool every store runs on your file. Here is how to read its errors, fix the most common ones, and get a clean pass before you upload to KDP.

html:
Before your ebook reaches a single reader, it has to pass a piece of software called EPUBCheck. It is the official validator for the EPUB standard, and every major store — KDP, Apple Books, Kobo, IngramSpark — runs it or something like it on upload. If your file fails, the store rejects it. This guide shows you how to pass EPUBCheck on the first try.

What EPUBCheck is checking

EPUBCheck reads your EPUB the way a store's ingestion system does and confirms it follows the EPUB specification. It looks at the container structure, the OPF package document, the navigation files, the manifest, and the XHTML inside each chapter. It does not judge your writing or your design — only whether the file is structurally valid.

Every issue it finds comes with a severity and a code. The severities that matter are Fatal and Error — these block acceptance. Warning and Info messages are worth reading but rarely stop an upload.

How to read an EPUBCheck error

A raw EPUBCheck message looks like this:

ERROR(RSC-005): ... attribute "opf:role" not allowed here

The code (RSC-005) tells you the category, and the text tells you what and where. The problem is that raw EPUBCheck output is written for developers, full of XML jargon and line numbers. Most authors don't need to decode it by hand. The free BookKraft AI EPUB Validator runs the same checks and translates each result into plain English with a suggested fix — no Java install and no command line.

The most common EPUBCheck errors and their fixes

Missing or broken navigation

If the NCX file or nav.xhtml is missing, out of date, or points at anchors that no longer exist, EPUBCheck flags it and the store's Go To menu breaks. Regenerate the navigation from your current chapter structure. See our reference on missing NCX navigation.

Manifest references to files that don't exist

RSC-007 means the OPF manifest lists a file that isn't actually in the package — usually because a chapter was renamed after export. Make sure every manifest entry points to a real file and every file is declared. Our guide to OPF manifest reference errors covers it.

Unescaped ampersands

EPUB chapter files are XHTML, so a literal & must be written as &. A raw ampersand in a title or heading causes an XML parse failure. This is extremely common in files converted from Word.

Unclosed tags

XHTML requires void elements like <img> and <br> to be self-closed (<img />). HTML5 lets them stay open; XHTML does not, so pasted web HTML often fails here.

Broken unique identifier

OPF-048 means the package's unique-identifier attribute doesn't point to a real dc:identifier element. Apple Books rejects this outright. Confirm the identifier id matches.

A workflow that passes on the first try

  1. Clean the manuscript first. Many EPUBCheck errors start as Word artifacts. The Kindle Format Fixer clears smart quotes, stray characters, and encoding problems before they reach the file.
  2. Validate early and often. Run the EPUB Validator as soon as you have a file, not just at the end. Fixing one structural issue sometimes reveals another.
  3. Fix in order of severity. Resolve every Fatal and Error result. Re-run after each round of fixes, since one repair can clear several messages.
  4. Re-validate the final file. Conversion tools can introduce new issues when they rebuild the EPUB, so validate the exact file you are about to upload.

A file with zero Fatal and Error results will pass ingestion on KDP and every other major store. For the complete list of what to check, work through our EPUB formatting checklist before you hit upload, and browse the EPUB errors reference for any specific code you run into.
